content:
maria-g: Hey folks, customer flagged that their SIEM ingest is missing a bunch of audit events from last night (token_revoked, key_access). Export job id `exp-20260316-09` shows completed but counts don't match the UI.
sam-lee: Can you paste the export job metadata and the timeframe? :eyes:
maria-g: timeframe is 2026-03-15T22:00Z -> 2026-03-16T04:00Z. Job metadata: `exp-20260316-09` -> src: audit-service, dest: s3://redwood-exports/customer-34/, forwarder: splunk-forwarder-v2, kms_key: alias/rdw-cust34. Size reported 1.2MB.
olivia_w: Did they confirm whether Splunk shows errors on ingestion? Sometimes the forwarder drops events if schema mismatches or timestamp parsing fails.
maria-g: Customer says Splunk index shows ~600 events but UI says ~3.2k for that window. They sent an example of an event that appears in UI but not in S3 export:

```
{"type":"token_revoked","user":"alice@example.com","ts":1679001203,"details":{"reason":"manual"}}
```

But their Splunk mapping expects `event_time` ISO string and `event_type` as top-level string, so maybe the forwarder was misconfigured.
kyle-r: Hmm, we recently rolled a forwarder change that renames `ts`->`event_time` and `type`->`event_type` only when `include_kms_metadata=true`. If the export job omitted KMS metadata because of a transient KMS error, the transform might have skipped those events.
sec-oncall-bot: alert: vault-kms request to alias/rdw-cust34 failed 2026-03-16T02:13:12Z with 503 from KMS. Correlates with job `exp-20260316-09` timeframe.
sam-lee: OK that matches. If forwarder depends on successful KMS fetch to add/transform fields, a KMS 503 could short-circuit mapping and push a reduced payload or drop records. Let's repro locally: @kyle-r can you run the export with `--force-include-kms=true` and tail the forwarder logs?
kyle-r: On it. I'll run a dry export against the same job id and compare counts. Quick repro command I'll use:

```
./tools/export_audit --job-id exp-20260316-09 --replay --force-include-kms=true --out ./tmp/replica.json
```

Then:

```
./tools/forwarder --input ./tmp/replica.json --config configs/splunk-forwarder-v2.yaml --dry-run
```

expect to see mapping errors in stdout.
maria-g: Customer asked for an interim workaround. Can we provide a query they can run via the API to pull the missing events until we fix the forwarder?
sam-lee: Yes: curl example to fetch events by type/time:

```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/events?start=2026-03-15T22:00:00Z&end=2026-03-16T04:00:00Z&types=token_revoked,key_access" \
  | jq '.' > events.json
```

that will return raw events in the canonical schema (no forwarder transforms). Share `events.json` with customer via secure link.
olivia_w: Also we should check retention/archival. The UI count discrepancy could be because some events were archived into cold storage and not included in the export job due to pagination bug. Ticketing note: add `retention_policy` and `archive_marker` checks in the export validation.
sec-oncall-bot: suggestion: escalate to eng-infra for KMS 503 correlation and to forwarder owners for schema resilience. Tagging @eng-infra on JIRA.
maria-g: Created JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENGSEC-4521 assigned to @sam-lee. Customer notified with API workaround and ETA 24h. :thumbsup:
